Article Title: Why has Shafali Verma been reprimanded by the ICC after India's win over Zimbabwe?
Article Text:
Shafali Verma (BCCI Photo)

What happened during the match?

One demerit point added to her record

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What is the penalty for a Level 1 breach ?

India vice-captain Shafali Verma has received an official reprimand for throwing the ball to the ground in frustration after dropping a catch during the second T20I against Zimbabwe.The incident took place during India's nine-wicket win in Raipur on Sunday. The 22-year-old was found guilty of breaching Level 1 of the ICC Code of Conduct.The incident took place in the 12th over of Zimbabwe's innings. Shafali dropped a catch offered by Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano at mid-off off Shree Charani's bowling. She then threw the ball to the ground in frustration.The ICC found that Shafali had breached Article 2.2 of its Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel. This rule deals with the “abuse of cricket equipment or clothing, ground equipment or fixtures and fittings during an International Match,” an ICC media release said.Along with the official reprimand, one demerit point has been added to Shafali's disciplinary record. This was her first offence in a 24-month period.Shafali admitted the offence and accepted the sanction proposed by G.S. Lakshmi of the ICC International Panel of Match Referees.As a result, there was no need for a formal hearing.On-field umpires Vrinda Rathi and Gayathri Venugopalan, third umpire Anna Harris and fourth umpire Janani Narayanan levelled the charge.Level 1 breaches of the ICC Code of Conduct carry a minimum penalty of an official reprimand. The maximum punishment is a fine of 50 per cent of a player's match fee, along with one or two demerit points.
Article Summary: India vice-captain Shafali Verma has received an official reprimand for throwing the ball to the ground in frustration after dropping a catch. The incident took place during India's nine-wicket win in Raipur on Sunday. The 22-year-old was found guilty of breaching Level 1 of the ICC Code of Conduct.

Article Title: Asian Para Games: Sheetal Devi, Swati Chaudhary storm into archery finals, eye gold medals for India
Article Text:
Sheetal Devi and Swati Chaudhary

Sheetal continues record-breaking run

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Mixed teams progress as India suffer individual setbacks

NEW DELHI: India's para archers Sheetal Devi and Swati Chaudhary stormed into the finals of their respective events at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Tuesday, assuring the country of at least two medals and setting up opportunities to add to India's tally.Defending champion Sheetal continued her impressive run in the women's compound category, defeating Japan's Shinohara Aya 145-137 in the semifinal. The 19-year-old will face Singapore's Alim Nur Syahidah in the gold-medal match on October 22.Swati, making her debut at the continental multi-sport event, also booked her place in the final after beating South Korea's Lee Eunhee 6-2 in the women's W1 semifinal. She will take on China's Mengkan in the gold-medal contest, with both Indian archers now assured of at least silver medals.Sheetal, who was born without arms and shoots using her feet and shoulder, has been one of India's standout performers in para archery. The Jammu and Kashmir archer equalled the world record and set a new Asian record during qualification, underlining her credentials as she seeks to defend her title.She continued her dominant campaign in the elimination rounds, defeating Hong Kong's Chan Yuen Wah 149-134 in the pre-quarterfinals and the Philippines' Agustina Bantiloc 147-135 in the quarterfinals before overcoming Shinohara in the last four.Sheetal had also produced a record-breaking 149 against Chan, surpassing the previous world record of 148 held by Britain's Jessica Stretton.The world No. 1 will now look to cap her campaign with another gold medal. She is also scheduled to compete in the compound women's doubles semifinals alongside Payal Nag.India also advanced to the semifinals in both the recurve and compound mixed team events. Paralympic gold medallist Harvinder Singh and Bhawna defeated Thailand 6-0 in the recurve mixed team quarterfinals, while Sheetal and Toman Kumar beat Japan 154-147 in the compound mixed team competition.However, the day brought disappointment in several individual events. Harvinder lost 5-6 to China's Yun Duo in a shoot-off in the men's recurve quarterfinals, while Bhawna went down 2-6 to Mongolia's Selengee Demberel in the women's last eight.In the men's compound event, Toman suffered a 144-149 semifinal defeat to China's Ai Xinliang and will compete for bronze. Shyam Sundar Swami had earlier lost 146-147 to Ai in the quarterfinals.With Sheetal and Swati now one victory away from gold, India will look to convert their strong performances into top-podium finishes as the para archery competition progresses.
Article Summary: Sheetal Devi and Swati Chaudhary reach the finals of their respective events at the Asian Para Games 2026. The 19-year-old will face Singapore's Alim Nur Syahidah in the gold-medal match on October 22. Swati, making her debut at the continental multi-sport event, also booked her place in the final after beating South Korea's Lee Eunhee 6-2 in the women's W1 semifinal.

Article Title: Sindhu, Mirabai in IOA electoral roll; Lovepreet’s doping past raises questions
Article Text:
Saikhom Mirabai Chanu

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Olympic and world medallists PV Sindhu and Saikhom Mirabai Chanu headline a star-studded list of athletes cleared to contest the Indian Olympic Association's (IOA) Athletes’ Commission elections on Nov 3, with weightlifter Lovepreet Singh’s doping past raising questions over his inclusion.The final electoral roll, approved by returning officer Sanjay K Srivastava, IAS (retd), also features Asian Games gold-winning hockey captains Harmanpreet Singh and Salima Tete, shooting sensation Neeru Dhanda, archery veterans Abhishek Verma and L Bombayla Devi, shot putter Tajinderpal Singh Toor, badminton's Kidambi Srikanth, fencer C A Bhavani Devi, rugby captain Nasser Aga Hussain and wrestler Aman Sehrawat.However, Lovepreet’s inclusion has drawn scrutiny. He tested positive for a prohibited substance at the senior Nationals meet in Visakhapatnam in Feb 2019 and was provisionally suspended by the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) in July that year. He later returned to competition, featuring at the 2022 CCWG in Birmingham.The Athletes' Commission eligibility declaration states: “I have never been sanctioned for a violation under the WADA Code or the NADA Act, 2022 or for a breach of any applicable integrity regulation”.His inclusion raises questions over the Indian Weightlifting Federation's (IWLF) nomination of his name and there's a high possibility that the electoral officer will cancel his eligibility and seek a fresh name.The draft roll, published on Oct 12, listed nominations from 19 NSFs. The final list has 17, with the Basketball Federation of India’s nominees Ram Kumar Gahlawat and Manisha Satyajit Dange, and the Kabaddi federation’s Balwan Singh and Mamatha, excluded.Of the 34 NSFs listed as IOA members, only 17 have nominees in the final roll. They are archery, athletics, badminton, bowling, cycling, fencing, handball, hockey, kayaking and canoeing, netball, rowing, rugby, shooting, squash, swimming, weightlifting and wrestling.The elections will determine athlete representation in the IOA’s Athletes’ Commission.
Article Summary: Olympic and world medallists PV Sindhu and Saikhom Mirabai Chanu headline a star-studded list of athletes cleared to contest the Indian Olympic Association's (IOA) Athletes’ Commission elections on Nov 3. The final electoral roll also features Asian Games gold-winning hockey captains Harmanpreet Singh and Salima Tete.

Article Title: Andrey Rublev opens up on mental struggles, says 'I was at the bottom of my darkest days'
Article Text:
Andrey Rublev (Image credit: X)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

ALMATY: Andrey Rublev has spent much of his career trying to get better at being Andrey Rublev. Now, the mercurial Russian, whose on-court meltdowns are almost as well chronicled as his title wins, is attempting to rewrite the script that took him to world No. 5.At 28, he is trying to become a different player. Rublev has slipped to No. 22, falling outside the top 20 for the first time since Jan 2020. For a player who finished each season inside the top 10 from 2020 to 2024, the decline is striking.Yet, after 10 Grand Slam quarterfinal appearances without advancing to a semifinal, Rublev has come to a realisation — to build something new, he must first be willing to break down what got him here.“It’s not easy to change something that you know for all your life,” said Rublev, the No. 4 seed at the Almaty Open, an ATP 250 event. “It’s not easy to switch that, what brought you to No. 5 in the world for something else that you don’t really trust yet.”The forehand, Rublev’s biggest weapon, is a useful example. It’s a shot he could turn to under pressure almost without thinking.“I’m trying to change, on and off the court, mentally, things that have become a habit, that have already taken me to the limit, with what I could do with that,” he says, eyes fixed on the table before him.“Now, it’s the second part of (my) career where I try to do something different completely.”There is no guarantee the experiment will work. Rublev knows that as well as anyone.“Maybe it’s going to make the second part of my career better than my first part, or maybe not,” he says, lifting his gaze. “But at least I know I did something, I gave myself a chance.”“With the game I used to have, it will go down little by little until I cannot play anymore,” he says. “To be just top 30 for the next five-six years, for me, it makes no difference.”For the past 18 months, Rublev has been working with former world No. 1 Marat Safin, a partnership that has pushed the 28-year-old to address mental and emotional struggles that have led him to hurt himself physically on court.Asked what has changed most since working with Safin, Rublev does not begin with tactics or results.“I’m enjoying much more the life. I’m much more in peace with myself,” he says.It is a striking answer from a player whose intensity has long been one of the defining features of his tennis.“From the past, before Marat, I was very depressed, and taking antidepressant pills to not feel depression,” he says.He pauses, taking a deep breath, before describing how low he had felt.“Basically, it was a bit of drama that was happening to me, and I didn’t know how to escape. I was at the bottom of my darkest days.”It was there, he says, that he reached a point at which he could no longer continue as he had been. He faced a choice, to remain trapped in the same patterns or to try, finally, to do something about them.“I choose to try to fix it,” he said.Rublev is not short of reminders that reinvention is possible.“When you see players like Sasha (Zverev) or Daniil (Medvedev), when they're doing something good, it gives a clear signal that I can do it as well,” he says. “Because I know what I'm capable of. If he can do it, I can find a way as well.”
Article Summary: Andrey Rublev is trying to become a different player. The Russian has slipped to No. 22, falling outside the top 20 for the first time since Jan 2020. Rublev has been working with former world No. 1 Marat Safin, a partnership that has pushed him to address mental and emotional struggles.

Article Title: China’s stapled visa row costs Arunachal weightlifter shot at World Championships
Article Text:
India China

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: Another sporting flashpoint in India-China ties has cost weightlifter Charu Pesi a shot at the world stage, with the Indian Weightlifting Federation (IWLF) withdrawing the Arunachal Pradesh athlete from the upcoming Senior World Weightlifting Championships in Ningbo after Chinese authorities indicated that he would be issued a stapled visa.Sources told TOI that the Chinese Visa Application Service Centre (CVASS) here sought an undertaking from the Indian federation confirming Pesi’s acceptance of the visa.The IWLF consulted government officials, who maintained that India does not recognise stapled visas issued by China to residents of Arunachal Pradesh. The federation subsequently decided against sending the men’s 65kg lifter to the championships, which begin on Oct 24.An eight-member Indian squad, led by Olympic medallist Mirabai Chanu , is scheduled to compete in Ningbo, with visa processing for the rest of the contingent continuing as usual.Unlike a regular visa stamped on a passport, a stapled visa is issued on a separate piece of paper. Beijing’s practice of issuing such visas to Arunachal Pradesh residents reflects its refusal to recognise India’s sovereignty over the region. India has consistently rejected the practice, viewing it as a challenge to its territorial integrity.This is far from an isolated incident. In July 2023, three Arunachal Pradesh wushu athletes, Nyeman Wangsu, Onilu Tega and Mepung Lamgu, were issued stapled visas for the Summer World University Games in Chengdu. India protested and withdrew its entire wushu contingent.The dispute resurfaced ahead of the Hangzhou Asian Games later that year, when the athletes faced entry and accreditation hurdles, preventing them from competing.For the lifter, it is a bitter setback. The championships would have offered valuable international exposure, with crucial ranking points at stake in the qualification race for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
Article Summary: Charu Pesi will not compete at the Senior World Weightlifting Championships in Ningbo. Chinese authorities indicated that he would be issued a stapled visa. Beijing’s practice of issuing such visas to Arunachal Pradesh residents reflects its refusal to recognise India's sovereignty.

Article Text:

Sonipat's Winners

Sonipat’s Gold Medal Winners [13]

When Kushal Dalal picked up boxing gloves, his family didn’t say no. When he gave that up and decided on archery – because Kushal didn’t like the idea of hitting anyone and felt at home in “a peaceful sport” – they agreed to that, too. There was no place around to practise archery, so a section of the family’s 5-acre farmland at Siwanka village in Sonipat was cleared. Paddy straw was woven to give him targets.Village gossip had brought Kiran Pahal’s running days to an abrupt end. After talk of Kiran “speaking to a boy” reached her father, he stopped her from going out. He relented after Kiran went on a hunger strike. Her grandmother used money from her pension to buy her a pair of running shoes.Before Neha Goyal played hockey for India, she helped her mother and sisters fix bicycles. Neha was eight when a friend told her hockey players got free shoes, clothes and notebooks. Her mother, who worked in houses and at a foam factory, didn’t stop her from playing.At the recently concluded Asian Games in Japan’s Aichi-Nagoya, a neighbour of Delhi reaped possibly India’s biggest harvest for a single city. Each of these stories – and 10 more like these – culminated in a gold medal.Each began, and blossomed, in Sonipat.Though in NCR, Sonipat doesn’t have Delhi’s influence, Gurgaon’s money or Noida’s infrastructure. As a manufacturing hub of auto components and ancillaries that are used in the domestic market and abroad, Sonipat has so far been writing its script, literally, in parts.Sport, which bubbles in its DNA, works much in the same way – many individual parts that don’t get to show their prowess as a sum. Aichi-Nagoya was that rare instance when they did. Serendipity? Perhaps. Organisation? Possible. Talent? Certainly.But talent needs spotting. And for virtually all the gold medallists, that was someone in the family who made it possible, sometimes with a push, sometimes with a quiet sacrifice –a family clearing land, a grandmother spending her pension, a mother working to buy shoes, a coach paying school fees for a stranger’s daughter.The other aspect of the Japan feat that places Sonipat apart from traditional sporting nurseries like Bhiwani (boxing) is the diversity of the 13 (individual and team combined) gold medals that athletes from here won, across disciplines like hockey, archery, kabaddi , athletics and wrestling.Serendipity did play a part. For several of these medallists, sport wasn’t the original dream. Neha Goyal, midfielder in the gold-winning women’s hockey team, started going for hockey classes after a friend told her hockey players received free shoes, clothes and notebooks. She joined because her family needed those things. Some families saw sport as a way to support the child’s education; others came to see it as a route eventually to a govt job.Coaches TOI spoke to said access to proper training remains the difference between a talent lost and a talent realised. Sonipat’s sportspersons have certainly benefited from its concentration of sports institutions and training centres around Rai and Bahalgarh. It has a Sports Authority of India (SAI) National Centre of Excellence, a residential sports school and Sports University of Haryana . The SAI centre covers 83 acres and its listed facilities include a 70-metre archery field, a floodlit synthetic athletics track, synthetic hockey fields, two mud kabaddi courts, wrestling halls, a sports injury and rehabilitation centre, a hypoxic chamber and hostels.Motilal Nehru School of Sports at Rai, founded by Haryana govt in 1973, has athletics, archery, weightlifting, wrestling and swimming among its competencies.Village akharas, kabaddi nurseries and private academies sit in different parts of the access route. One such academy, run by former India hockey captain Pritam Rani Siwach and her husband, has produced a steady stream of national hockey players. Seven hockey players from Sonipat were part of the men’s and women’s Indian teams that won gold at Aichi-Nagoya: four women and three men. All four women and one in the men’s team (Pritam Rani’s son Yashdeep) trained at the academy, which now has around 200 players, 150 of them girls.Among the youngest there is Ritika. The five-year-old is still mastering her numbers and alphabets in school but is quickly picking up dribbling and promptly agreed to show this reporter the right grip for the hockey stick. “Aise pakadte hain. Aur phir ball ko goal mein daalna hota hai. Jo ball andar daalega, woh jeetega! (this is how you hols the stick. The objective is to score a goal with the ball. Whoever does that wins)” she said.When Pritam Rani started the academy in 2004, she had seven trainees. When the academy paid school fees and helped buy shoes and other equipment, more began to join. I never wanted money to become the reason a talented girl stopped playing,” she told TOI. Food mattered, too. Many girls came from families for whom milk and fruit were luxuries, so the academy began providing soaked chana, milk and bananas.Neha, who came for the shoes, stayed for the dream – of building a house for her mother. “I did not start playing hockey thinking I wanted to play for India. I was in Class IV when a friend told me about the shoes, clothes and notebooks,” she said. “There were people who told my mother to keep me at home. But she never stopped me.” A cash prize for being player of the match changed her attitude towards hockey. “That Rs 2,000 changed something inside me. I started thinking if I played well, I could earn. Then on, hockey was not just a game for me. It became my responsibility,” she said.Abhishek Nain’s first reason for playing hockey was less ambitious. He was nine when he followed a classmate to a ground because it was an excuse to bunk. His father,, asked him to consider quitting hockey – which he was playing at the national level – after a series of injuries and focus on getting a govt job. Coaches persuaded the family to let him continue. Years later, at Aichi-Nagoya, he would score India’s winning goal against Pakistan in the Asiad semi-final.Seeing girls running on a track outside her school drew Kiran into athletics so much that she began sprinting in her school shoes and slippers, sometimes even barefoot. “I did not know where this would take me or that I would one day be wearing the India badge. I just liked running and wanted to try.” She joined Indian Railways in 2021, gaining financial stability after years of training. “For an athlete, knowing that there is a secure job gives a lot of confidence,” said Kiran, who won the 4x400m relay team gold in Japan.Meenu Beniwal, president of Haryana Olympic Association, linked Sonipat’s sporting culture to shrinking landholdings and search for livelihoods beyond farming. “As ancestral landholdings have shrunk and farming has become less viable for many families, sports have emerged as an important pathway to secure govt jobs and build a better future,” she said. Proximity to Delhi and recruitment opportunities in the Army, Railways, paramilitary forces and other central government departments have also encouraged young people to pursue sport, she felt.Sports University of Haryana vice-chancellor Ashok Kumar said ambitious parents have helped build the ecosystem by investing their own money and taking risks for their children. Institutions have added to that support, creating a baseline sporting infrastructure framework in the city. The university admitsstudents each year, and Sonipat accounts for aroundof admissions.Kabaddi player Pardeep Narwal says children in villages such as Rindhana grow up watching neighbours, relatives and seniors succeed in the sport. Local grounds and kabaddi academies run by former players bring large numbers of youngsters into the sport. In Rindhana alone, around 300 children practise across three grounds, he said.“From my village alone 25-30 athletes have played in Pro Kabaddi League,” Narwal said. Seeing other athletes succeed encourages more children in the village to try. “Family members motivate the kids. They look at a neighbour’s son succeeding and ask their own children why they can’t do the same,” he said.Wrestler Naveen Mor describes the same process in akharas, with local dangals giving children competitive experience early. “When an entire community encourages a sport, the chances of producing champions naturally increase,” said Mor, who runs a wrestling academy on a one-acre plot near Murthal, where he trains 70-80 children. He said he does not charge them because talent may emerge from families unable to afford expensive coaching.“Many of our athletes come from humble farming families, where children grow up helping with physical work and learn discipline, endurance and the value of hard work early in life. Wrestling also offered generations of youngsters from middle-class families a way to build a career, earn recognition and secure a govt job.Earlier, choices for many such families were limited, and sports became a route to a better future. Over time, this created a strong sporting culture, with akharas, coaches, families and former wrestlers all contributing to the next generation,” Mor said.The same may now be happening for hockey and athletics. Maybe, it takes a village to keep producing gold medallists.Women’s HockeyNeha GoyalJyotiSakshi RanaShilpi DabasMen’s HockeySumitAbhishek NainYashdeep SiwachAthleticsKiran PahalArcheryKushal DalalKabaddiSunil KumarAshu MalikRajraniWrestlingSujeet Kalkal
Article Summary: Sonipat, in Haryana, won 13 gold medals at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. The city is a manufacturing hub of auto components and ancillaries that are used in the domestic market and abroad. For virtually all the gold medallists, that was someone in the family who made it possible.

Kolkata: Three players from Jharkhand will be part of India’s four-member lawn bowls squad for a historic three-Test series against New Zealand in Nov, part of the centenary celebrations of sporting ties between the two countries.Lawn bowls is one of the only four sports, alongside cricket, hockey and football, selected for the centenary programme.2022 Commonwealth Games silver medallists Dinesh Kumar and Sunil Bahadur and rising player Reshma Kumari, all from Jharkhand, have been selected alongside Arjuna Awardee and Commonwealth Games gold medallist Pinki Singh for the series, scheduled from Nov 16-18 in Auckland.“This is a very important event for us because only four sports are taking part in the centenary celebrations. On the days we are playing, no other sport will be taking place, which means we will receive exclusive coverage,” Bowling Federation of India president Ravi Bengani told TOI in an exclusive interview on Thursday.India will play three Test matches over three days, with each Test comprising five matches — men’s pairs, women’s pairs, mixed fours, mixed pairs 1 and mixed pairs 2.The New Zealand series is part of a broader international exposure programme the federation has put in place as it begins preparations for the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.A 12-member Indian contingent will travel to Malaysia later this month for a World Bowls-sanctioned tournament, while another group will compete in an invitational event in Hong Kong, where Indian players won bronze medals last year.The federation’s confidence has also received a boost from Putul Sonowal’s recent podium finish at the Champion of Champions event, a first for an Indian player at the prestigious competition.“We have decided to participate in as many World Bowls-sanctioned events as possible. International exposure is crucial if we want to bridge the gap with the leading nations,” Bengani said.The federation is also planning to strengthen its support structure through its partnership with Bowls New Zealand. Bengani revealed that India currently does not have a dedicated national coach, making the proposed knowledge-sharing programme particularly significant.“We have signed an agreement with Bowls New Zealand and now we will have more exchange programmes. We will bring their coaches and technical officials to India and provide our players with greater exposure and expertise,” Bengani said.The plans have gained momentum following the federation’s recognition by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports earlier this year, a move expected to improve funding and access to high-performance support.As far as the 2030 Commonwealth Games are concerned, the federation has set ambitious targets. “I’m committing to at least four gold medals for India in 2030. Personally, I feel we can win even more if we continue on the current path,” Bengani said.With a packed international calendar, plans to bring in New Zealand coaches and technical experts, and Ahmedabad 2030 on the horizon, the federation believes Indian lawn bowls is entering its most ambitious phase yet.
Article Summary: Lawn bowls is one of the only four sports, alongside cricket, hockey and football, selected for the centenary programme. India will play three Test matches over three days, with each Test comprising five matches. The series is part of a broader international exposure programme the federation has put in place as it begins preparations for the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.

Article Title: EFI mess costs Indian riders global stage, FEI ban from Dec 1
Article Text:
Equestrian Federation of India

New Delhi:

Yet another tale of administrative chaos and athletes paying the price. Caught in a prolonged governance crisis at the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI), Indian riders now face a ban from international competitions, with their sporting futures hanging in the balance. The latest setback comes at a time when the govt is pushing to bring more international events to India and widen Indian athletes’ exposure to global competition.The International Equestrian Federation (FEI) has decided to suspend the EFI from Dec 1 over prolonged governance irregularities and failure to hold fresh elections, effectively shutting Indian riders, officials, trainers and horses out of international events. TOI is in possession of FEI’s Oct 15 letter confirming the decision, which was taken at the international body's board meeting on Oct 13.Explaining its move, the FEI said the EFI’s prolonged governance crisis had reached a tipping point. “The absence of elections to date to elect a new Executive Committee, has resulted in a prolonged governance and leadership irregularity that is no longer sustainable,” the letter by FEI Governance Director Francisco Lima stated.The crisis follows the Delhi high court’s dissolution of the EFI executive committee in Feb 2026. Its elected tenure had expired in Sept 2023, while fresh elections remain pending nine months after the court’s intervention. The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) constituted an ad hoc committee on March 27 to oversee the federation and facilitate the electoral process.While acknowledging the committee’s Sept 27 submission and its work, the FEI said elections were expected by Jan 31, 2027. However, the suspension will be reviewed only after the polls are held and evaluated by the international body.The consequences are sweeping. Citing its statutes, the FEI said the EFI “may not attend or be represented at any session or meeting of any FEI body, nor may it organise international events.” More damagingly, athletes, officials, trainers and horses “may not participate in international events organised by the FEI or any other national federation, whether under the Indian flag or the FEI flag.”With the suspension taking effect before the stated election deadline, Indian riders risk losing crucial international competition opportunities. Their return will depend on the completion of elections and the FEI’s subsequent evaluation, leaving athletes caught in a governance crisis they did not create.
Article Summary: The International Equestrian Federation (FEI) has decided to suspend the EFI from Dec 1 over prolonged governance irregularities and failure to hold fresh elections. Indian riders now face a ban from international competitions, with their sporting futures hanging in the balance. The latest setback comes at a time when the govt is pushing to bring more international events to India and widen Indian athletes' exposure to global competition.

Former Australia captain Steve Smith has been cleared of concussion and resumed fielding duties on the fifth day of the first Test against South Africa at Kingsmead in Durban on Tuesday, after undergoing a series of clinical assessments following a blow to the helmet.The 37-year-old batter was struck by a short-pitched delivery from Anrich Nortje during Australia's second innings. Smith attempted to duck under the ball but misjudged its trajectory as it failed to rise as much as he expected.Although he continued batting after the incident, scoring 27 off 41 balls before being caught at long-on off Simon Harmer, Smith did not take the field when South Africa began their second innings on Monday. Michael Neser served as his substitute fielder during that session.However, Smith returned to the field on Tuesday morning after being cleared under Cricket Australia's concussion protocols. He was stationed in the slip cordon when South Africa resumed their chase and subsequently took a catch to dismiss Kyle Verreynne off Matt Renshaw's bowling."Steve Smith has undergone a series of clinical assessments over the past 24 hours in accordance with Cricket Australia’s concussion protocols and has been cleared to take the field this morning," Cricket Australia said in a statement.The incident brought back memories of Smith's previous concussion scare during the 2019 Ashes in England, when he was struck on the head by fast bowler Jofra Archer and forced to miss part of a Test match.Smith's return to the field came after medical assessments over the preceding 24 hours, with Australia following the prescribed protocols before allowing the experienced batter to resume his duties.His presence was a boost for Australia as they pushed for victory in the series opener, with South Africa mounting a determined resistance on the final day.South Africa resumed at 102/4 on Tuesday, needing another 319 runs to win. They reached 166/6 by lunch after Australia struck twice to strengthen their grip on the contest.Opener Aiden Markram led the home side's resistance, remaining unbeaten on 69 at the interval alongside Marco Jansen on seven. The pair had to rebuild after Wiaan Mulder's patient 69-run fifth-wicket partnership with Markram ended when Josh Hazlewood had Mulder caught behind by Alex Carey.Part-time spinner Matt Renshaw then dismissed Verreynne, who made just one before edging a reckless shot to Smith at slip.Renshaw has been Australia's standout performer with the bat, having scored 190 in the first innings and 82 in the second, before adding two wickets to his match contribution.Australia needed four more wickets at lunch to seal victory in the opening Test. The second Test of the series is scheduled to begin in Gqeberha on Sunday.

Smith took a catch to dismiss Kyle Verreynne off Matt Renshaw's bowling. Australia needed four more wickets at lunch to seal victory in the opening Test.

Article Title: ‘Give Vaibhav Sooryavanshi harsh truth’: Ex-India cricketer explains Gautam Gambhir, management’s approach
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Gautam Gambhir

Kartik draws comparison with Yashasvi Jaiswal

‘You have to wait for your opportunity’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Should Vaibhav Sooryavanshi be included in the playing XI despite established players' performances? Yes, he deserves a chance No, the current players should retain their places Only if an established player is underperforming 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s continued absence from India’s playing XI has left fans frustrated, but former India spinner Murali Kartik believes there is little reason for the team management to rush the 15-year-old into the side when the established opening options are performing well.Despite being named Player of the Series during India’s tour of Zimbabwe, Sooryavanshi did not feature in the subsequent T20I series against Afghanistan and West Indies. The teenage batter is also yet to make his senior India debut on home soil, even as his performances in the IPL have made him one of the country’s most talked-about young talents.His absence has become a talking point at India’s home matches, with supporters hoping to see him play. Sooryavanshi did get an opportunity to open alongside Abhishek Sharma during the Asian Games, offering a glimpse of his potential, but his wait for a regular spot in the senior team’s playing XI continues.Speaking in an interaction facilitated by Sony Sports Network, Kartik backed the management’s decision to retain its existing opening combination, highlighting the contributions of Sanju Samson and Abhishek. He also pointed to the presence of Ishan Kishan , whose recent form has made competition for a place at the top of the order even tougher."I am not somebody who makes a change for the sake of it. I know change is constant, but change for the right reasons.There has to be a reason why there is a change. So, when it comes to the opening duo in India, I know they are a bit inconsistent, but that is what has won games for you," said Karthik.Samson and Abhishek have accumulated 1,125 runs together in 38 T20Is, making them India’s fourth-highest run-scoring partnership in the format. Kartik believes their record, combined with the quality of the other available batters, makes it difficult to justify a change simply to accommodate another promising player."We have seen the quality of Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma, both of them are sitting right up there. Then you've got Ishan Kishan, who's your number two, number one players out there, so it's very difficult to make the change."Kartik also compared Sooryavanshi’s situation with that of Yashasvi Jaiswal, who has found opportunities limited in India’s white-ball setup despite producing impressive performances in Test cricket and the IPL.With Rohit Sharma and Shubman Gill established at the top of the order in ODIs, Jaiswal has had to wait for his chance in the format. Kartik sees a similar challenge for Sooryavanshi, whose talent is not in question but who must contend with players already occupying the positions he is targeting."Yes, we get excited because he's an exciting talent. We are not taking anything away, but at the end of the day, it's like Yashasvi Jaiswal in white-ball cricket. Do you make the change just for the sake of it, just to knock somebody off?""I don't think I am in favor of that. I've never been in favor of that. I don't think going forward I'll ever be in favor of that," said Karthik.The former spinner stressed that a player’s ability alone does not automatically justify a change in the playing XI. In his view, selection decisions must be based on a clear need rather than the excitement surrounding a young prospect.Kartik acknowledged that Sooryavanshi’s opportunity could come if one of the established batters goes through a prolonged lean patch. The youngster made his India debut in England when Samson was struggling for runs, illustrating how changes in form can open doors for players waiting on the sidelines.However, Kartik said there was no way to predict when such a situation might arise. Until then, Sooryavanshi must remain prepared to step in whenever the team needs him.At the end of the day, we can't predict what's going to happen. Tomorrow, it could be that one of the batters going 15 innings without getting runs, and you are forced to make a change."So, at that point of time, you want the second guy who's waiting. The guy waiting behind the door, ready to come out and say, 'listen, I'm there.'""And that's exactly how it should be handled, rather than saying, oh, we like him, people want to see him, so let's bring him in. No, that's being unfair on the guys who are already there," said Karthik.Beyond selection, Kartik believes it is important for the team management to be honest with Sooryavanshi about his position in the squad. He pointed to the messages from head coach Gautam Gambhir and captain Shreyas Iyer , who have stressed that the youngster must remain patient and consistent with his preparation.Kartik said that while hearing such a message might be difficult for a player eager to prove himself, being told the truth is better than being left uncertain about his future."Even if you have to give them the harsh truth, it's better to give it to them, because you take it on your chin. You might not like it; it's not palatable for a while, but it is what it is. You have to deal with it and move on.""I think that is the best way to go about things. Because Shreyas has spoken about it, Gautam has spoken about it, I'm pretty sure they're having the right word with Sooryavanshi, because he's there. Nobody is saying that he's not there. It's just that sometimes when the others are doing well, you cannot. It is unfortunate, but it is what it is," said Karthik..
Article Summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is yet to make his senior India debut on home soil. The 15-year-old was named Player of the Series during India’s tour of Zimbabwe. Former spinner Murali Kartik believes there is little reason for the team management to rush the youngster into the side.

Article Title: Ranji Trophy: Sachin Yadav, Karan Lamba miss double tons by six runs each after 338-run stand
Article Text:

JAIPUR: If Day One was about building a foundation, Day Two turned into a relentless exhibition of dominance by Sachin Yadav and Karan Lamba that ended in uncanny heartbreak. In a rare cricketing coincidence, both batters missed out on coveted double centuries, falling agonizingly six runs short of the landmark on identical scores of 194 in Rajasthan 's Group ‘D’ Ranji Trophy fixture against Railways at the Sawai Man Singh Stadium here on Monday.Resuming from the overnight score of 247/2, the Rajasthan duo continued to dictate terms before Sachin’s dismissal sparked a post-lunch collapse as the hosts eventually folded for 497 all out.The final session belonged to the hosts’ bowlers. Debutant pacer Danish Bhambu impressed with his disciplined line and length, finding good support from Chetan Sharma and left-arm seamer Akash Singh.On a pitch that was still playing well, the seam trio did an excellent job of squeezing the run flow. However, it was left-arm spinner Mohit Changra who provided the hosts with their first breakthrough, trapping opener Vivek Singh lbw.At stumps, Railways were 46/1, trailing by 451 runs.Earlier, Karan, playing his 11th First-Class game, completed his third Ranji hundred in no time, ensuring another long day for the Railways’ bowlers. The sheer scale of the dominance even sparked some tongue-in-cheek chatter in the visiting dressing room. With the scoreboard ticking away relentlessly, a few in their camp jokingly muttered, "Yeh kya pitch banwaya hai (what kind of a wicket has been readied)?"Reflecting on the surface, Karan noted, "You rarely get wickets like this in domestic cricket.The pitch was favoring batting. I tried to stay put and play a long innings."The morning session brought its own test when the new ball was introduced, making life tricky for the batters. Edges flew, but Railways were let down by poor fielding as a couple of catches went down. Weathering the storm, Sachin and Karan expertly defended and left the probing deliveries.Once the early threat wore off, they unleashed their strokes. Sachin compiled his 194 off 358 balls with 22 fours and four sixes, while Karan matched him brick-for-brick with a 194 off 284 deliveries, laced with 19 fours and 2 sixes.Having trained together for years at the Rajiv Gandhi Cricket Academy, the duo’s deep understanding was evident on the field as they shared a partnership of 338 runs. "We know each other's strengths," Karan shared. "Our communication was very easy because we have played cricket together for years."Together, their marathon alliance completely broke the back of the Railways attack. Sachin was eventually stumped, while Karan holed out at point. Admitting to the disappointment of missing the double ton, Karan said, "It was on my mind a little bit, but not too much," he added.
Article Summary: Sachin Yadav and Karan Lamba share a partnership of 338 runs to power Rajasthan to 497 all out. Sachin was eventually stumped, while Karan holed out at point. At stumps, Railways were 46/1, trailing by 451 runs.

Article Title: Ranji Trophy: Chinmay Sutar creates history with unbeaten 400, becomes only second Indian to reach the milestone

MUMBAI: Mumbai batter Chinmay Sutar made history on Monday when, playing only his second first-class fixture, the 29-year-old slammed 400 not out, in an marathon innings spanning 517 balls and studded with 46 fours and seven sixes, in a Ranji Trophy Plate group match between Mizoram and Nagaland at the Nagaland Cricket Stadium in Sovima.During his epic knock, Sutar, who played one match (against Maharashtra) in the Vijay Hazare Trophy for Mumbai last season, went past Prithvi Shaw 's 379 to record the second-highest score in the history of the Ranji Trophy, and joined BB Nimbalkar, who had scored 443 not out for Maharashtra against Kathiawar in 1948-49 to become only the second Indian batsman to score 400 in a first-class match, and the 10th overall.Sutar was within touching distance for the all-time record for the Ranji Trophy's highest-ever individual score, held by BB Nimbalkar, Unbeaten on 392 at tea, Sutar reached 400 in the 155th over, with Mizoram declaring the innings at 581 for nine immediately after the No. 3 bat reached the special milestone.Sutar put on an unbeaten 190-run partnership for the tenth wicket with Lalrempunia Chhakchhuak, who made 14 not out off 76 balls.Such was the impact of Sutar's knock that the second highest score in Mizoram's innings was Jehu Anderson (69).Riding on Sutar's colossal knock, Mizoram made 581 for nine declared. Sutar had fallen run out on 99 on his first-class debut in the previous round against Manipur at Nadiad.Chinmay's father Rajesh Sutar is a former Mumbai off-spinning allrounder who once opened the batting with the legendary Sachin Tendulkar for Mumbai. He played seven first-class matches.Chinmay Sutar played for the India Under-23 team in the 2019 ACC Emerging Teams Asia Cup in Bangladesh.Sutar has been one of the top run-getters in the past two seasons of T20 Mumbai, thus playing a stellar role in Maratha Royals’ back-to-back title wins in this period.Sutar scored half-centuries-62 off 49 balls & 61 off 52 balls for Maratha Royals in the semis and finals of the 2026 T20 Mumbai League, eventually finishing with 210 runs.In 2025, he was the ‘Orange Cap’ winner in the T20 Mumbai League.
Article Summary: Mumbai batter Chinmay Sutar made history on Monday. Sutar slammed 400 not out, in an marathon innings spanning 517 balls and studded with seven sixes, in a Ranji Trophy Plate group match between Mizoram and Nagaland. He joined BB Nimbalkar, who had scored 443 not out for Maharashtra against Kathiawar in 1948-49 to become only the second Indian batsman to score 400 in a first-class match.

Former India opener Aakash Chopra believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi faces an uphill battle to break into India’s T20I playing XI, with the team’s established top-order options leaving little room for the 15-year-old to feature.Sooryavanshi is part India’s squad for the upcoming five-match T20I series against New Zealand, which begins on November 22. However, the teenager was not given a single opportunity during the recently concluded home series against the West Indies, which ended in a 2-2 draw.Chopra feels the youngster’s absence from the playing XI is primarily a result of the lack of available slots rather than a question of his ability. He suggested that rotating the top-order batters could be a way to give Sooryavanshi opportunities, although he acknowledged that the idea has not found much support.Speaking on his YouTube channel, the former India batter was asked whether Sooryavanshi should replace Tilak Varma in the XI, given the latter’s perceived inconsistency."Vaibhav Sooryavanshi isn't getting chances because a place isn't getting created for him. In whose place should you play him? To be fair, he can play only in place of Sanju Samson Abhishek Sharma , or Ishan Kishan ," Chopra responded."When three people are doing well, you can't get a chance suddenly. I know it is heartbreaking, but there is no other way. No one is agreeing with the method I am suggesting. You can do a rotation. Give chances to all four of them in rotation," he added.Chopra also argued that keeping Sooryavanshi in the squad without giving him any playing time throughout the series would serve little purpose. In such a situation, he believes the teenager should be released to play in the Ranji Trophy instead.The youngster has made an encouraging start to his T20I career, scoring 246 runs in eight matches at a strike rate of over 186, including two half-centuries. Despite his impressive numbers and reputation for aggressive batting, he has yet to get a consistent opportunity in the current international setup, with the more experienced Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma preferred at the top of the order.Chopra also defended Tilak Varma, disagreeing with the suggestion that the Indian vice-captain has been underperforming and should make way for Sooryavanshi."If you say Tilak Varma doesn't perform at all, then what you are saying is slightly wrong. Tilak Varma struck two centuries when he played at No. 3. After that, he got injured and had a slight problem before the World Cup," he said.The former India opener pointed to Tilak’s contributions in the middle and lower-middle order, arguing that his recent performances should not be overlooked simply because he has not always batted at his preferred position."The World Cup didn't start well, but after that, ever since he became a finisher, he has done a good job, whether you see the performances in the Asian Games or now. The fact is that he has been doing really well in the middle order and the lower-middle order. So I feel shooting arrows at Tilak Varma is not right," Chopra observed.
Article Summary: Former India opener Aakash Chopra believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi faces an uphill battle to break into India’s T20I playing XI. Mohammed Shami ’s continued omission from India’s plans has raised fresh questions, with former India cricketer Mohammad Kaif calling for greater transparency from the selectors following the announcement of the squad for the upcoming series in New Zealand.The BCCI announced India’s squads earlier this week for the New Zealand tour, which includes two Tests, five ODIs and five T20Is. However, the absence of the experienced fast bowler from the squad has drawn criticism, particularly in view of his domestic performances and past contributions to the national team.Kaif believes the selectors owe Shami an explanation, given the pacer’s achievements and his crucial role in India’s run to the 2023 ODI World Cup final. Shami finished that tournament as the leading wicket-taker, claiming 24 wickets in just seven matches.“No questions are asked, no BCCI selector explains the decisions, there’s no accountability. You’ve to keep transparency. This is about Mohammed Shami – the player of the 2023 world cup. If he wasn’t there, India would not have reached the final. When Hardik Pandya got injured, Shami came in and didn’t make you feel the absence of a sixth bowler.If Shami wasn’t there, India would’ve been searching for a sixth bowling option. Rohit Sharma took India to the final with five bowlers because Shami was the backup," Kaif said on Cricbuzz.The former India batter also pointed to Shami’s performances in domestic cricket, arguing that the pacer has continued to make a case for himself despite being away from the international setup.“Shami took 22-23 wickets in Indian conditions. So, I feel there has to be some transparency why the decision has been taken. He’s doing everything – playing first-class cricket, Ranji Trophy, taking wickets," he added.Shami last represented India in March 2025 during the Champions Trophy triumph. His most recent Test appearance, meanwhile, came in the World Test Championship final against Australia in June 2023.The fast bowler has since been attempting to regain his place through domestic cricket following an extended absence from the longest format. Concerns over his match fitness have reportedly been a key factor behind the selectors' reluctance to include him in the Test squad, with questions remaining over his ability to withstand the demands of red-ball cricket.Shami has also been bowling short spells in domestic matches, a factor cited in discussions over his omission. Kaif, however, questioned whether that should be a decisive consideration, pointing to the workload management followed for India’s pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah.“I heard that he’s (Shami) bowling short spells and so not being picked. Jasprit Bumrah also bowls four-over spells in Test cricket. In England, his workload was being managed and Shubman Gill followed it. If one bowler is being treated in a particular way, then the same can be done for others too. There’s nothing wrong in bowling short spells if you can get the job done. So, transparency remains a grey area which I hope should be addressed soon.Someone has to give the clarity," Kaif said.The debate over Shami’s selection has gained another dimension following the latest squad announcement. The pacer was subsequently rested from Bengal’s second-round match in the ongoing Ranji Trophy season, adding to the uncertainty surrounding his immediate return to competitive cricket.With India preparing for the New Zealand series, Kaif’s comments have brought the focus back on the selectors’ assessment of Shami’s fitness and readiness, as well as the need for greater clarity over decisions involving one of the country's most experienced fast bowlers.
Article Summary: Mohammed Shami has been left out of India's ODI and T20 squad for New Zealand tour. Former India cricketer Mohammad Kaif has called for greater transparency from the selectors. Kaif believes Shami should be given an explanation for his omission.

Article Title: ‘SMS Stadium is my fortress’: Sachin Yadav’s KL Rahul-inspired celebration after ton
Article Text:
Sachin Yadav

Jaipur: It was far from an ideal opening Ranji Trophy match for Sachin Yadav, who scored just 1 and 0 against Tamil Nadu last week, but the left-hander did not put a foot wrong on Sunday. The opener expertly negotiated a tricky opening hour of Day One against Railways in Rajasthan 's Group ‘D’ fixture at Sawai Man Singh (SMS) Stadium, anchoring the innings to reach his second First-Class century with an unbeaten 115 off 221 balls.The milestone arrived when he deftly pushed a delivery from seamer Adarsh Singh to third man for a sharp single. The moment triggered an ecstatic celebration, a passionate leap into the air, followed by a nod to KL Rahul’s style as he drew a circle on the pitch and firmly stomped his bat right in the centre. Playing in only his fifth First-Class match, the young opener proved exactly why he is highly regarded, striking 15 fours and two sixes.Alongside Karan Lamba, with whom he stitched a partnership of unbeaten 157, Sachin ensured the day’s honours belonged to the hosts. Rajasthan reached 247/2 when stumps were called nearly an hour early due to a hailstorm.Karan, a centurion in the previous match, picked up right where he left off and looked well on his way to another hundred, sitting unbeaten on 89 (122) with nine fours and two sixes.Sachin considers the ground his fortress. “I consider SMS Stadium as my fortress because I made my debut here and a lot of my good knocks have come here.That is why I did that particular celebration which I took from KL Rahul’s books to communicate that this is my place,” he said after the day’s play.The left-hander focused on playing session by session. “The overcast conditions gave the bowlers some initial movement. My strategy was just to bide my time instead of rushing into things,” he said.Earlier, after opting to bat first, Rajasthan received an early reprieve when opener Rohan Rajbhar was dropped off Adarsh Singh in the third over. However, he failed to capitalise on the lifeline, scoring 11 off 34 balls before seamer Kunal Yadav induced a catch to mid-off in the 13th over.One-down batter Sumit Godara’s brief stay was highlighted by two sixes off spinner Toufik Mondal. Looking to build on his 49 against Tamil Nadu, he hit 25 off 47 balls before being trapped lbw by Railways skipper Bhargav Merai just 15 minutes before lunch.Throughout the day, Sachin remained a calming presence at the crease. The 22-year-old holds a promising pedigree, having scored a magnificent 130 against Delhi and a 92 on debut last season against Mumbai. Supported by Lamba, who survived a late slip drop off Zubair Ali on 7, the duo guided the hosts safely through to the forced stoppage.“Tomorrow we will look to negotiate the first hour and hopefully we will again dominate the opponents,” Sachin added.
Article Summary: Rajasthan reach 247/2 when stumps were called nearly an hour early due to a hailstorm. Sachin scored his second First-Class century with 115 off 221 balls. Karan Lamba was unbeaten on 89 (122) with nine fours and two sixes.

Article Title: 11.46 RPO, 13 wides, 18 extras: India’s pace attack under pressure ahead of New Zealand tour
Article Text:
India's Arshdeep Singh celebrates with teammates (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What is the biggest challenge for bowlers in the current series? Flat pitches Heavy dew Short boundaries Inconsistent execution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Bengaluru: When batters are scoring at 11.46 runs an over, even quality bowling attacks can be made to look ordinary. India’s T20I series against the West Indies has exposed the vulnerability of the hosts’ pace unit, with flat pitches, dew and short boundaries proving a punishing combination for bowlers.West Indies’ stunning 250-run chase in Ranchi, completed with nine balls to spare, prompted a stern assessment from India head coach Gautam Gambhir.“These bowlers are our bowlers, not someone else’s bowlers. Their careers are at stake,” he had said, underlining the scrutiny facing the attack.With the exception of Indore, where India successfully defended 223, the bowlers struggled to contain a fearless West Indies batting line-up. While the absence of Jasprit Bumrah and, to an extent, Hardik Pandya has been felt, the bigger concern for the team management is the inconsistency shown by Arshdeep Singh, Mayank Yadav and Prince Yadav.The two young quicks, Mayank and Prince, have alternated between brilliance and waywardness during the series, highlighting the challenges of adjusting to different match situations. The fourth T20I in Hyderabad offered a clear example.India conceded 18 extras, including 13 wides. Arshdeep accounted for six, while Mayank and Prince leaked two and one, respectively. Their attempts to execute wide yorkers and fuller deliveries repeatedly missed the mark, allowing the West Indies batters to maintain the pressure.India’s lack of proven T20 pace-bowling depth has consequently become a talking point. That has put renewed focus on the return of Bhuvneshwar Kumar, whose recall after nearly four years away from the national side could prove timely.The experienced swing bowler has enjoyed a productive run in the IPL, taking 45 wickets across the last two seasons. More importantly, his success has been built on control and execution rather than sheer pace, qualities that India’s younger quicks have often lacked in this series.Conditions, however, have offered little respite to bowlers. High-scoring surfaces and heavy dew have meant that even small lapses have come at a significant cost.As India prepare for a demanding tour of New Zealand, they know the challenges ahead will be very different. The pitches may offer more assistance, but the key question remains whether the bowling group can quickly adapt and improve its consistency.On the eve of the rain-affected series finale in Bengaluru, fast-bowling coach Morne Morkel urged observers to consider the physical and mental demands placed on modern cricketers.“We sometimes forget that mental fatigue plays a big part. We have to manage that and be smart with it. Some of the players went for the Asian Games and then straight into a full series against the West Indies. These guys are also human,” Morkel said.“Execution and skills become better when you’ve recovered, slept well and mentally refreshed. That’s a challenge. We’re going to New Zealand now and it’s a jam-packed schedule there as well,” he added.There was, however, one encouraging sign. All-rounder Naman Dhir grabbed his opportunity after replacing Washington Sundar in the XI.
Article Summary: Flat pitches, dew and short boundaries are punishing combination for bowlers. India's lack of proven T20 pace-bowling depth has become a talking point. Bhuvneshwar Kumar's return after nearly four years away from the national side could prove timely.

What is para powerlifting?

Ashok's journey

India's Ashok won the silver medal in the men's 65kg powerlifting event at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Tuesday.The 37-year-old lifted 192kg to finish second behind China's Zou Yi, the reigning Paralympic champion, who won gold with a lift of 216kg. Indonesia's Margono claimed bronze after lifting 177kg.Ashok started the competition with a successful 187kg lift. He then improved his performance to lift 192kg in his second attempt.However, he could not lift 201kg in his final attempt and finished with a best lift of 192kg.Para powerlifting is a bench press event that tests an athlete's upper-body strength. Athletes compete in different weight categories, but the sport has only one discipline.The sport is open to athletes with impairments in their hips or legs.Ashok hails from Gohana in Haryana's Sonipat district. He contracted polio as a child and went on to compete in para powerlifting at the international level.

Article Title: 'I wanted to win this gold for my mother': Rinku Hooda triumphs amid grief at Asian Para Games
Article Text:
Para javelin thrower Rinku Hooda (ANI Photo)

'I wanted to win gold for my mother'

From a farming accident to the Asian Para Games podium

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Paralympic medal remains the ultimate target

The pain of losing his mother was still fresh, and a shoulder injury had disrupted his preparations. Yet, when Rinku Hooda stepped into the arena at the Asian Para Games, he had one goal in mind, to win gold for the person he had lost.The 27-year-old Indian para-athlete fulfilled that promise on Monday, clinching the men's javelin throw F46 gold with an effort of 65.11m. He edged compatriot Ajeet Singh, who secured silver with a throw of 65.02m, while Indonesia's R Saktyono took bronze with 55.30m.For Rinku, however, the medal was about much more than a place on the podium. It was a tribute to his mother, who passed away on August 8, leaving him to navigate personal grief while preparing for one of the biggest competitions of his season."I was a little disturbed in the last two months. My mother passed away August 8. I am still disturbed. It's okay from outside but it's not the same inside," Rinku told PTI from Nagoya."I wanted to win this gold medal for my mother. So, I would like to dedicate this gold to my mother."Rinku barely had time to come to terms with the loss before returning to training. After completing the 13-day mourning period, he resumed preparations on August 19, initially keeping the intensity low."It happened on August 8. And on August 19, as soon as the 13th day (mourning period) was over, I started training. But I started lightly," said Rinku, who trains at the Rajiv Gandhi Stadium in Rohtak.His preparations suffered another setback when he sustained a Grade 1 shoulder tear, forcing him to rest for around 20 days. The injury has since healed, although he continues to use taping as a precaution."I had an injury on my shoulder, a Grade 1 tear. Then I rested for around 20 days. I have fully recovered from the injury. Earlier, I used to do taping and stuff. I still do taping, but I didn't feel any pain," he said.Rinku's journey in sport began against difficult circumstances. At the age of three, he lost his left arm in a farming accident when it became trapped in a paddy-sowing machine, eventually requiring amputation.The setback did not take away his passion for sport. While helping his father with farm work, Rinku continued participating in school-level state running competitions. His introduction to javelin came through Amit Kumar Saroha, an Indian para-athlete who has mentored and coached several young talents.Rinku announced himself on the international stage with gold at the Youth Asian Games in 2015, followed by silver at the World U20 Para Athletics Championships in Switzerland in 2016. He also competed at the Rio Paralympics that year, finishing fifth at just 18.His medal collection has since grown steadily. He won bronze at the 2018 Asian Para Games and silver at the 2022 edition in China. At the World Para Athletics Championships, he claimed silver in 2023 before winning gold in 2025.The F46 classification is for athletes with a single above- or below-elbow amputation, or an equivalent impairment.Despite his success at continental and world level, one achievement continues to elude Rinku, a Paralympic medal. He finished fifth at the Paris Paralympics in 2024, and the experience has strengthened his resolve to return to the podium at the 2028 Los Angeles Games."I have not won a medal in the Paralympics. So, that is my target now. I will focus more on that. The qualification for the 2028 Paralympics will start five to six months before the Games," he said.
Article Summary: Rinku Hooda won gold in the men's javelin throw F46 at the Asian Para Games. The 27-year-old lost his left arm in a farming accident at the age of three. He finished fifth at the Rio Paralympics in 2016 and won silver at the 2022 Games.

NEW DELHI: India made a spectacular start to the Asian Para Games, collecting 11 medals, including four gold, across shooting, athletics, judo and swimming on Monday to occupy fourth place in the overall standings.Established stars Mona Agarwal and Nishad Kumar led the charge, while middle-distance runner Soumya and javelin thrower Rinku also finished on top of the podium. India celebrated three 1-2 finishes, with compatriots sharing the gold and silver medals in shooting, athletics and javelin.The opening day also brought encouraging news from archery, table tennis and badminton, with Sheetal Devi matching the world record in the women’s compound qualification round and several Indian paddlers and shuttlers assuring themselves of medals by reaching the semifinals.The medal rush began with a stirring comeback from Mona in the women’s 10m air rifle SH1 final. The Paris Paralympics bronze medallist climbed from sixth place to set an Asian Para Games record of 250.0 points, edging compatriot Avani Lekhara by just 0.4 points.Avani, the defending champion and a two-time Paralympic gold medallist, settled for silver with 249.6 points, giving India its first 1-2 finish of the day.Mona topped qualification with 629.1 points, setting an Asian Para Games qualification record, while Avani was second with 626.4.The victory also secured India a second quota place for the 2028 Los Angeles Paralympics. Mona had already earned one quota at the World Shooting Para Sport World Championships in Changwon, South Korea, last month, where she won silver.The athletics arena delivered three gold medals and a series of podium finishes as India continued its strong start.Nishad, a two-time Paralympic silver medallist, produced a memorable performance to win the men’s T47 long jump with an effort of 7.11m. It was the Indian’s first international competition in the long jump, making his gold medal all the more special.Nishad lost his right arm in an accident involving a grass-cutting machine when he was six years old. He nevertheless dominated the competition, recording 7.11m twice to finish ahead of Uzbekistan’s Omadbek Khasanov, who won silver with a season-best 6.99m.Soumya added another gold in the women’s 1500m T12/T13 event, clocking a personal-best 5:12.39. Ajeet Singh followed closely with 65.02m, also a season best, to take silver. He clocked 56.68 seconds to finish behind Uzbekistan’s Egor Bolotov, who won gold in 52.90 seconds. Article Title: ‘Our captain’: Portugal FA president backs Cristiano Ronaldo’s return for the second time despite suspension and Jorge Jesus fallout

Ronaldo reportedly left Portugal after Jesus allegedly broke promises over his Norway warm-up, with a private apology replaced by public defiance/ Image: X

November could offer Ronaldo a route back

Soccer Football - Saudi Pro League - Al Nassr v Al Diriyah - Al Awwal Park, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia - October 9, 2026 Al Nassr's Cristiano Ronaldo celebrates scoring their first goal REUTERS/Hamad I Mohammed

The federation wants him back, but the decision remains unresolved

Cristiano Ronaldo’s future with Portugal looked uncertain after he walked out of the national-team camp during the October international break, but the federation has now made clear that it wants its captain back. President Pedro Proença has publicly backed the 41-year-old despite his provisional suspension and fallout with head coach Jorge Jesus, with November’s Nations League fixtures offering a possible route back.Speaking at a Portuguese Football Federation event in Funchal, Ronaldo’s birthplace, Proença reaffirmed the forward’s standing in the national team and described him as a central figure in Portuguese football.“We are in the home of the greatest asset Portuguese football has ever produced: Cristiano Ronaldo, our captain,” Proença said, as quoted by ESPN. “Our captain, Cristiano Ronaldo, is one of our key pieces.”This is not the first time FPF president Pedro Proença has publicly backed Ronaldo and called for his return to Portugal. In a surprising U-turn just hours after the federation’s disciplinary proceedings became public on Saturday, October 10.The federation had initiated proceedings on Friday, October 9, following Ronaldo’s abrupt departure from Portugal’s camp during the October international break after a dispute with Jorge Jesus over his playing time. Ronaldo was provisionally suspended, with a final punishment yet to be announced.However, Proença quickly shifted the focus towards reconciliation, making the federation’s desire for Ronaldo’s return unmistakable. In comments relayed by Italian journalist Fabrizio Romano, he said: “The federation, the coach and all of Ronaldo's teammates are of one mind, we want Ronaldo back.”“I expect Ronaldo to return during the international break next November, and he is also eager to return, he is the best player of all time,” Proença added.Ronaldo’s departure followed a disagreement over his role during Portugal’s recent camp. The forward believed Jesus had failed to honour an understanding about his playing time, and left the squad without permission.The situation was especially awkward because Ronaldo and Jesus had worked together at Al-Nassr last season, winning the Saudi Pro League title before being reunited with Portugal. The fallout has now placed their relationship under scrutiny, even as the federation signals that it wants the captain available again.The FPF initiated disciplinary proceedings earlier this month, on October 9, and announced the case publicly the following day. It classified the matter as urgent and referred it to the Disciplinary Investigation Committee. The federation said Ronaldo had initially faced an automatic provisional suspension after leaving camp without permission, before a separate preventive suspension was ordered as the proceedings began.Ronaldo has acknowledged that he must accept the consequences. In his public statement, he said he would accept whatever punishment the federation decides, while making clear that he has not abandoned his international career and remains willing to represent Portugal after serving any suspension.Portugal’s next matches are scheduled for November, when the team faces Denmark on November 14 before travelling to Wales three days later. The side has already secured its place in the Nations League quarter-finals after winning its opening four matches, but Ronaldo’s availability remains dependent on the disciplinary process and the decisions of Jesus and the federation.Proença’s expectation that Ronaldo will return during the November international break gives the captain a possible path back, although it does not amount to confirmation that he will be selected. The next squad announcement should offer a clearer indication of whether the dispute is beginning to ease.There is also a personal milestone in play. Portuguese journalist Miguel Pereira previously told talkSPORT that Ronaldo wanted to score his 1,000th career goal for Portugal rather than Al-Nassr, giving the target a potential international significance. With Ronaldo having reached 981 career goals following his recent AFC Champions League Elite strike for Al-Nassr FC, he sits just 19 goals away from the historic four-figure mark.The upcoming international windows will continue to provide critical opportunities to pursue that ultimate ambition in national colours.Proença’s public support suggests Portugal’s leadership is not treating the walkout as the end of Ronaldo’s international career. The disciplinary case remains open, and any return will still depend on the eventual sanction, the coach’s selection and Ronaldo’s willingness to rejoin the squad.For now, the federation has stated its position plainly: it wants its captain back. November’s fixtures will show whether that welcome can translate into Ronaldo’s return to the Portugal team.
Article Summary: Portugal FA president Pedro Proença backs Cristiano Ronaldo’s return, calling him ‘our captain’ despite his suspension and dispute with Jorge Jesus. The federation initiated disciplinary proceedings earlier this month, on October 9, and announced the case publicly the following day. Ronaldo was provisionally suspended, with a final punishment yet to be announced. November could offer Ronaldo a route back, with the Nations League offering a possible route back.

Article Title: Amid riots and looting, France makes big call on PSG vs Barcelona Champions League showdown

PSG and Barcelona meet in crucial Champions League clash

Paris Saint-Germain’s UEFA Champions League clash against Barcelona will go ahead as scheduled on Tuesday in Paris, despite a wave of protests, riots and looting across France that has prompted authorities to consider localised curfews and tighten security.French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez confirmed the decision after an emergency meeting with senior government officials, saying the possibility of postponing sporting events had been discussed but that it would not affect Tuesday’s fixture at the Parc des Princes.“But this does not apply to tomorrow's match between PSG and FC Barcelona,” Nuñez said, adding that other matches scheduled in European competitions this week would not be affected.The decision comes amid a tense security situation across the country, with violence targeting city halls, public buildings and businesses and more than 2,000 arrests reported. French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has instructed prefects to impose “very limited” and “localized” curfews in areas at risk of further unrest.Tuesday’s fixture is a major European contest, with PSG hosting Barcelona at the Parc des Princes in the Champions League league phase.Both sides have won their opening two matches and will look to maintain their perfect records.The fixture will require a robust security deployment, with police forces already stretched following weeks of student protests. In May, Paris police detained dozens of people after violence disrupted celebrations following PSG’s second Champions League title win, while a group also attempted to storm a police station in the capital.The French government is preparing for heightened security around the fixture after a weekend of violence and looting across the country. Businesses and public buildings were targeted, while authorities acknowledged that the unrest had overwhelmed police in some areas.Nuñez admitted that authorities had “lost control” in some major cities on Saturday, when hundreds of businesses were looted.The Interior Minister offered his resignation on Sunday, but President Emmanuel Macron asked him to remain in office to address police requirements during the emergency.Macron also instructed Nuñez “to take all necessary steps to ensure full transparency about the failures in planning and intelligence-gathering that led to the violence.”Meanwhile, Lecornu said details of the areas that would be placed under curfew would be announced later. Despite the unrest, the government has decided not to postpone the PSG-Barcelona clash.
